content: 1. Encorafenib affects the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose by half (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 225 mg/day). After discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives, resume the previous encorafenib dose. 2. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate, should be avoided. After discontinuing the moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives, resume the previous entrectinib dose. 3. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 5. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of ergotamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate, erythromycin lactobionate, and erythromycin stearate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. 9. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 12. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens and esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Estrogens are CYP3A4 substrates, and their efficacy in hormone replacement therapy may be reduced. 13. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of estropipate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of etoposide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and etravirine decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 18. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of everolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration of fedratinib, a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate, with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors. 20. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal formulations) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 22. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of finasteride by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 24. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 25. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 26. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of gepirone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the gepirone dose by 50% when used concomitantly with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 31. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half of the recommended dose if co-administered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 34. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of ibrutinib and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. 37. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 38. Fosaprepitant decreases the effects of ifosfamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for ifosfamide neurotoxicity (e.g., visual and auditory hallucinations, somnolence, confusion, delirium) if combined with fosaprepitant. Consider also monitoring for decreased ifosfamide efficacy. 39. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and iloperidone increases the levels of fosaprepitant. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 40. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of imatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 41. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of imipramine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Fosaprepitant decreases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of isradipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 48. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 49. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosaprepitant also increases the levels or effects of itraconazole. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 50. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, thus increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. 52. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib.
